title: Why Highway Guardrails Have Heavy End Boxes 🤯
topic: Why highway guardrail ends feature a heavy steel box designed to flatten and redirect guardrail beams during a crash.
claims: Guardrail end terminals (extruder terminals) flatten and curl steel W-beams upon impact.
Plastic deformation of the guardrail absorbs the kinetic energy of a crashing vehicle.
Extruder terminals are engineered to redirect the flattened beam away from the roadway to prevent vehicle spearing.

title: Why Your Funny Bone Shocks You ⚡
topic: Why bumping your elbow's funny bone triggers an intense electrical shock down your forearm.
claims: The ulnar nerve runs close to the surface at the elbow joint.
Impact on the ulnar nerve produces a tingling or electric shock sensation down the forearm.
Lack of thick muscle and fat padding over the ulnar nerve at the elbow makes it vulnerable to direct compression.

title: Why Car Windshields Have Black Dots 🤔
topic: Why car windshields have tiny black dots along the outer edges (the frit pattern)
claims: The black border and dots on a windshield are a ceramic paint called frit.
Frit helps bake the adhesive that bonds the windshield to the car frame.
The dot pattern (halftone) helps distribute thermal stress to prevent the glass from cracking due to temperature differentials between the dark ceramic and clear glass.

sources.cite: Öztürk et al. (2024), Bulgarian Chemical Communications. doi:10.34049/bcc.56.3.ik-m
sources.claim: The black border and dots on a windshield are a ceramic paint called frit.

sources.cite: Lundevall et al. (2018), Applied Adhesion Science. doi:10.1186/s40563-018-0111-6
sources.claim: Frit helps bake the adhesive that bonds the windshield to the car frame.

title: How Mosquitoes Bite You Without Pain 🦟
topic: How mosquitoes pierce your skin without triggering pain receptors
claims: Mosquitoes use a fascicle containing a labrum, mandibles, and maxillae to pierce skin.
Mosquito saliva contains compounds with anesthetic properties that numb the feeding site.
The bending and micro-serration of the proboscis reduce mechanical stress on skin mechanoreceptors.

sources.cite: Wahid et al. (2007), The Open Entomology Journal. doi:10.2174/1874407900701010001
sources.claim: Mosquitoes use a fascicle containing a labrum, mandibles, and maxillae to pierce skin.

title: Why Fingers Prune, Pineapples Sting, and Sharks Live 400 Years
topic: weekly: Why Fingers Prune In Water 💧🧽, Why Tuna Meat Is Red Meat While Cod Is Pure White 🐟🥩, Why Fresh Pineapples Eat You Back 🍍
claims: Pruney fingers are an active nervous system reaction causing vasoconstriction, as studied by Changizi (2011) and Kareklas (2013).
Myoglobin color determines red vs white muscle tissue in fish and land animals based on aerobic endurance demands.
Bromelain in fresh pineapple digests proteins and is denatured by heat during cooking or processing.
Greenland sharks have extremely low metabolisms and can live for centuries, as radiocarbon-dated by Nielsen (2016).
Onions release syn-propanethial-S-oxide via lacrimatory factor synthase which irritates eyes, while garlic releases allicin which does not.
Buoyancy of watermelons is due to overall average density being lower than water due to trapped air and porous rind structure.
Potato tubers respond to temperature and humidity cues that shift the balance of abscisic acid and gibberellins to break node dormancy.
The ulnar nerve runs close to the elbow surface without muscle padding, causing electric shock sensations upon compression.

sources.claim: Bromelain in fresh pineapple digests proteins and is denatured by heat during cooking or processing.

title: How Tuning Forks Actually Make Sound 🔊
topic: Why tuning forks require two identical prongs to make sound instead of a single metal rod
claims: Tuning forks have two prongs that vibrate in opposite directions, creating a balanced mechanical system that minimizes stem vibration.
A single metal rod vibrates differently and lacks the counter-balancing motion of paired prongs.
Scissors use a shearing mechanism created by two crossing blades rather than a single downward wedge.

title: The Hidden Cause Of Brain Freeze 😮
topic: What actually triggers a sudden 'brain freeze' when you consume cold food too fast
claims: Brain freeze (sphenopalatine ganglioneuralgia) is caused by rapid cooling and warming of the palate capillaries.
The pain is referred pain, misinterpreted by the trigeminal nerve.
The trigeminal nerve carries sensory signals from the face and mouth to the brain.
Pressing the tongue against the palate is a widely accepted technique to alleviate the sensation by providing warmth.

title: Why Ponds Don't Freeze Solid 🤔
topic: Why Backyards Ponds Do Not Freeze Solid When It Is -15 °C Outside
claims: Water reaches its maximum density at approximately 4 °C (39 °F).
Liquid water cooler than 4 °C becomes less dense and rises toward the surface, freezing into an insulating layer of ice.
The ice layer acts as a thermal insulator, preventing the underlying water from freezing solid and allowing aquatic life to survive.
Watermelons float because their overall average density is lower than that of liquid water.

title: Why Heat Treating Makes Steel Hard 🤯
topic: Why Metal Becomes Significantly Harder and Stronger When Heat Treated
claims: At room temperature, iron atoms form a ferrite crystal structure where planes can slip past each other.
Heating iron transforms it into austenite, dissolving carbon atoms in the face-centered cubic structure.
Rapid quenching freezes the carbon in place, forming martensite, which is a stressed body-centered tetragonal structure that resists dislocation movement and increases hardness.

sources.cite: Wijnen et al. (2025), Materials & Design. doi:10.1016/j.matdes.2025.113698
sources.claim: At room temperature, iron atoms form a ferrite crystal structure where planes can slip past each other.
